caption:
Whisky or whiskey? 🥃 Which spelling is right, and why there are two.

Whisky (no “e”): Scotland, Canada, Japan, India. Scotch’s spelling is even written into law.
Whiskey (with an “e”): Ireland and the USA, mostly. A few American brands still print “whisky”.
The popular story: in the 1800s Irish distillers kept the “e” to stand apart from Scotch, and America followed the Irish. Spellings only settled in the early 1900s.
Both come from the Gaelic uisge beatha, “water of life”.
